reviewerRole: Independent visual reviewer; no product code edits
reviewScope: Actual rendered three-way macro comparison plus front and oblique context; technical regionalColor failure investigated separately

threeWayComparison.r01: Frozen reference appearance; nearly uniform vermilion colour remains the unresolved material problem.
threeWayComparison.r02CompositingOnly: Visually close to R01, clean; no obvious new blotches, gross hue shift or lost texture observed. Visual gain is small. Retention depends on independently proven compositing correctness, not a claim of significant beauty improvement.
threeWayComparison.r02AdditionalOuterTransition: Softens and washes out the coloured border around Cupid bow and lower outer lip, with a slight perceptual narrowing of vermilion. No clear compensating increase in natural surface organization. Not recommended as default or as a necessary new art control.

observations: The first-candidate broad blotches are gone; removing a failed addition is not an improvement over original R01.
Macro and oblique beauty show an edge preference change, not a substantial quality advance.
Whole-face beauty shows no clear material improvement at ordinary portrait scale.
No severe newly formed halo is claimed. Rejection is based on insufficient benefit and mildly reduced boundary readability.
Perceived narrowing describes colour coverage, not a claim that geometry changed.
recommendedAction: Keep only compositing correction if its technical gate establishes necessity and compatibility.
Remove added edge transition or leave it disabled; do not retain a new default control just because it exists.
Continue to list spatial colour organization and inner-lip dynamic continuity as unresolved major issues.
notEstablished: Significant improvement to lip realism or whole-person quality.
Resolution of nearly uniform painted vermilion.
Physical/anatomical correctness of material or movements.
limits: Images describe the second candidate only; no future source revision has been visually approved.
Technical completion and publication are separate from this visual review.
